newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian call money rate down 50 bps to 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian call money rate down 50 bps to 10 pct.

text.p: Croatia's benchmark call money rate fell 50 basis points to 10 percent on Thursday on the unusually high supply of kuna funds, dealers said.
"We've seen a strong rise in supply of kuna funds, and because of that the interest rate on call money loans fell to 10 percent from 10.5 percent," Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
Blagaic said there was over 85 million kuna of fresh funds on offer against the demand of 13.5 million, which was fully met in the morning trade.
Of those, call money loans accounted for 13 million, and the rest was one two-month loan granted to a savings bank at 18 percent a year.
The overnight trade totalled 30.2 million, as one bank borrowed to maintain its mandatory reserves and one had shortfalls. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
